newsitem.title: USA: Calif. water slide park reopens after deadly accident.
newsitem.headline: Calif. water slide park reopens after deadly accident.

text.p: A California amusement park will reopen Saturday less than two weeks after a water slide accident killed one teen-ager and injured 32 others, city and park officials said.
Waterworld USA in Concord, California, about 30 miles northeast of San Francisco, was closed down after part of a 40-foot-tall winding slide collapsed on June 2.
Teen-agers on the slide plummeted to the ground, turning the pool of water below red with blood. One teen-age girl died and many other teens broke bones in the fall.
Experts brought in to inspect the park after the accident concluded the park was safe, Concord Mayor Bill McManigal said in a statement Friday.
"After extensive and thorough inspections by a number of experts, we are pleased to announce that the park will reopen," the mayor said.
